title: Question 1.1
statement_text: Is it true that for any finite family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$ that contains at least one forest, there exists a constant $k_0 = k_0(\mathcal{F})$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is $k$-nice for all $k \geq k_0$?
context_text: For a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs and an integer $k\ge1$, $R_k(\mathcal{F})$ is the smallest $n$ such that every $k$-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy (as a subgraph, not necessarily induced) of some member of $\mathcal{F}$; $\mathcal{F}$ is $k$-nice (Ramsey-nice) if, for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=R_k(\mathcal{F})$ and every $k$-colouring of $E(G)$, there is a monochromatic copy of some $F\in\mathcal{F}$. This extends the question of Bialostocki and Gyárfás for tuples $(H_1,\dots,H_k)$; note that colours are not associated with specific members of $\mathcal{F}$ and $k$ is independent of $|\mathcal{F}|$. If no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a forest, then by Erdős' graphs of large chromatic number and large girth, $\mathcal{F}$ is not $k$-nice for any $k$. The question asks whether containing a forest is also sufficient, for all large $k$. The answer is easily yes for families containing a graph with at most $2$ edges. With $K_3$, $P_4$ (path on four vertices) and $S_3$ (star with three edges) the connected graphs with three edges, the authors show that $\{K_3,P_4\}$ is $k$-nice for every $k$, $\{K_3,S_3\}$ for every $k\ge2$ but not $k=1$, $\{P_4,S_3\}$ for all $k$ in an explicit set containing all large $k$ not congruent to $0$ modulo $3$ and all $k\equiv0\pmod 3$ except $3,6,18,21,24,30,33,39,42,51,66$; Garrison showed $\{P_4\}$ is $k$-nice for all $k\ne3$ and every star is $k$-nice for all $k$.

title: Conjecture 1.5
statement_text: Any finite family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$ that contains at least one forest is $k$-nice for infinitely many integers $k$.
context_text: For a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs and an integer $k\ge1$, $R_k(\mathcal{F})$ is the smallest $n$ such that every $k$-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy (as a subgraph, not necessarily induced) of some member of $\mathcal{F}$; $\mathcal{F}$ is $k$-nice (Ramsey-nice) if, for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=R_k(\mathcal{F})$ and every $k$-colouring of $E(G)$, there is a monochromatic copy of some $F\in\mathcal{F}$. This extends the question of Bialostocki and Gyárfás for tuples $(H_1,\dots,H_k)$; note that colours are not associated with specific members of $\mathcal{F}$ and $k$ is independent of $|\mathcal{F}|$. If no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a forest, then by Erdős' graphs of large chromatic number and large girth, $\mathcal{F}$ is not $k$-nice for any $k$. The authors ask whether every finite family containing a forest is $k$-nice for all sufficiently large $k$, and propose this weaker conjecture. With $K_3$ the triangle, $P_4$ the path on four vertices and $S_3=K_{1,3}$ the star with three edges, they prove that $\{K_3,P_4,S_3\}$ is $k$-nice for infinitely many $k$, and that for every $r\ge1$, every family consisting of $K_{1,r+1}$ together with graphs that each contain a cycle (with no bound on the number or size of the members) is $k$-nice for infinitely many $k$.

title: Question 1.8 (Gyárfás)
statement_text: Suppose that $G$ is the union of three triangle factors on the same set of vertices. Is $G$ 5-colorable?
context_text: This question arises in the analysis of the maximum chromatic number of unions of triangle factors, which is the main ingredient in proving item (3) of Theorem 1.3. A positive answer would imply that every 3-regular $n\times n\times n$ 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph contains a matching of size at least $\lfloor 3n/5 \rfloor$.
paper_contribution: The paper shows that a positive answer follows if either the Molloy–Reed conjecture or the Borodin–Kostochka conjecture is affirmed, and studies the question in the broader context of chromatic numbers of triangle-factor unions (Theorem 1.7).

title: Conjecture 1.10 (Aharoni, Charbit and Howard)
statement_text: In any $d$-regular $n \times n \times n$, 3-partite, 3-uniform hypergraph not containing repeated edges, there exists a matching of size at least $\left\lfloor \dfrac{d-1}{d}\, n \right\rfloor$.
context_text: This is Conjecture 9.3 from Aharoni, Charbit and Howard [1]. The conjecture is motivated by the question of finding large matchings in regular multipartite hypergraphs, and is related via Lemma 1.9 to bounding the chromatic number of unions of triangle factors.
paper_contribution: The paper disproves this conjecture by a large margin, constructing, for arbitrarily large $d$, $d$-regular $n\times n\times n$ 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraphs containing no matching of size larger than $2n/3$.
notes: PDF source — the bound in the statement is rendered as 'd 1/d n' with garbled floor symbols (PDF cid artifacts); reconstructed as $\lfloor (d-1)/d \cdot n \rfloor$ from context and the disproof discussion.
